Week 12 Waiver Wire Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 17: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs withe ball during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Bullock · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:01 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, the other wants to win – but loses anyway. The baby horses currently lead the all-time series, 33-15-1 thanks in great part to the Peyton Manning/Marvin Harrison Sr. years. However, Houston has won 5 of past 6, thanks to the Colts no longer showing interest in winning football. On paper, as of this writing, the Texans should absolutely dominate this game – and very well may. H-Town QB C.J. Stroud is having an MVP season. The Houston wide receiver corps is one of the best in the league – including the son of the aforementioned Harrison Sr.. Their run game ran away when Joe Mixon suffered the mystery of the ages injury in 2024, but Stroud has still managed to find ways to complete 201 passes for 2462 yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 INTs. The offensive line remains offensive, mostly, but has had just enough get-in-the-way-ness to give Stroud time to throw. Currently, the Texans passing attack is 4th overall. Defensively, Houston has the horsepower to compete at an elite level, but due to off-coverage, injuries and what looks to be confusion with the gameplan, they're currently ranked 20th. Some believe it's a little too much "read your own press coverage", others blame coaching and play calling. In some ways it seems a desire to change up from last season to keep opponents guessing has taken this defense away from what they do best. If you're great at zigging, but decide to zag all the time cause you think your opponent is expecting the zig, then you need to be ok with ignoring your own strengths… We won't talk about the special teams… #ulcerinducing Meanwhile, over in the baby horse stable, the Colts are clearly trotting down the rebuild trail. So far in 2026 Indy has: A new owner who has taken direct control over the coaching staff An interim general manager (after firing their previous one late last month) Quenton Nelson: Traded to the Seattle Seahawks. DeForest Buckner: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs: Traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Keenan Allen: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. And managed to win 1 game since all these team-affecting moves. Their current goal seems to be the #1 draft pick, if the Los Angeles Chargers don't beat them to it. Colts vs Texans predictions: In true Houston Texans fashion, the Texans will beat an opponent who doesn't want to win. Just as they did to the aforementioned Chargers. The 2026 brand of Texans football doesn't defeat winning teams (exception: the Jacksonville Jaguars cause, #Glitter). They do, however, lose the battle to not win – meaning when an opponent wants to lose, they freely allow H-Town to go to town on them. Which will happen again tonight. Stroud will look like an MVP candidate on a national stage. The Colts will show all their dysfunction. And the talking heads will ignore the apparent incoming mutiny on Kirby Drive. Indianapolis Colts 13 Houston Texans 38 Those with a superficial knowledge of the Texans will beat the drum that they still have a shot at the playoffs, and how they've fixed their issues. Until the following week when they lose against the Baltimore Ravens at the end of the month. Meanwhile, those who do lift the hood and look beyond the check engine light glaring on this franchise's dashboard will see a different prediction: The end game pot is on the stove, simmering away. Chances are tonight will turn the burn down just long enough to have a nice Thanksgiving.

This is a tough blow for the Colts, who seemed to have found something in McGowan, the rookie running back out of Kentucky. away.headline: Shane Steichen says Colts have not shut down Alec Pierce for the season
away.blurb: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature. Pierce has not played since aggravating a heel injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2 and the Colts' recent roster moves have made it clear that they have shifted their attention to the 2027 season. While that may be the case, head coach Shane Steichen said on Monday that the team has not made any call about whether Pierce will return in their final six games. "I know there's reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season," Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. "We have not made that determination. He's still going through his rehab process. The only way we'll put him out there is if he's 100 percent. We gotta be really smart." Pierce has a short window to get to 100 percent before the season is over and bringing him back from a long layoff may not be the best way to ensure that he's at full strength for next season, so it may just be a matter of when rather than if the Colts ultimately decide to shut the wideout down until next year.

The Colts on Wednesday ruled out tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), tackle Bernhard Raimann (concussion), defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf), tackle Jalen Travis (knee) and cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. (knee) for Thursday night's game against the Houston Texans. Slated to host a divisional game against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, the Bills ruled out defensive starters Christian Benford and Dorian Williams due to injuries. Meanwhile, the Dolphins will have plenty of backups on the offensive side of the ball on Sunday. Starting running back Devon Achane and quarterback Malik Willis are both unavailable. That means Ollie Gordon will shoulder the bulk of the work on the ground while former Syracuse starter Kyle McCord fills in at quarterback. In other Bills' news on Saturday, defensive tackle Ed Oliver woke up with oblique discomfort. As a result, Buffalo added him to the official injury report with a questionable tag. When did Tre'Davious White rejoin Bills? After starting 16 regular season games last year , White, a 2017 first-round pick by Buffalo, failed to garner overwhelming interest on the free-agent market. With the Bills keeping only three true outside cornerbacks on their 53-man roster, it always made sense to bring White back as an insurance policy, and they finally did on October 19 . "We brought Tre back here, if given the opportunity, to go in there and help us play winning football. I thought he played really good football at the end of last season," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady. away.headline: Miami Dolphins news roundup: Week 11 injury report includes Aaron Brewer update
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins will be without punter Bradley Pinoin on Sunday as they face the Buffalo Bills. Pinion has a right groin injury and missed practice all week before being ruled out on Friday's injury report. Miami signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad this week and is expected to elevate him to the active roster by today's 4 p.m. Eastern deadline. Miami also ruled out wide receiver Jared Wayne for Sunday's game. He has a quadriceps injury. The Dolphins injury report included cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee) and safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), both doubtful for the game. Cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee), center Aaron Brewer (concussion), and cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. (toe) are all questionable. Brewer, who missed last week's game with the head injury, fully participated in practice on Friday and, as long as he has no symptoms on Saturday, should be cleared to play. The Bills side of the reports includes cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) having been ruled out of the game while tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful. Safety Damar Hamlin (toe), defensive tackle T.J. Sanders (defensive tackle), and tight end Jackson Hawes (shoulder) are all questionable. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

picks.blurb: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2). Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Week 12 Waiver Wire 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 Neal Coolong · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Soldier Field in late November isn't where a 3-6 team usually goes to turn its season around, but the New Orleans Saints are still one game behind Carolina in the NFC South. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: Irish kicker Charlie Smyth signs new New Orleans Saints deal after NFL comeback
away.blurb: Irish kicker Charlie Smyth signs new New Orleans Saints deal after NFL comeback - Irish Star irishstar Load mobile navigation News Politics It has been a rollercoaster journey for the Mayobridge man, who was released by the Saints in August before being retained on their practice squad through the NFL's International Player Pathway programme Sport By Eamon Doggett 12:03, 22 NOV 2026 County Down's Charlie Smyth has signed a new deal with the New Orleans Saints to join their active roster. Given another chance earlier this month, after the Saints released fellow kicker Daniel Carlson, Smyth converted three field goals, including a 48-yard effort, in a dramatic 23-22 overtime victory over the Cleveland Browns at the Caesars Superdome. Smyth followed that up with an impressive 55-yard field goal against the Carolina Panthers last weekend, although New Orleans suffered a heartbreaking 20-17 defeat on the final play of the game. The NFL rules state that a practice squad player can only be elevated to the active roster three times during a season before they are required to sign to the active roster to feature again. But now 25-year-old Smyth has secured his place on the Saints' main roster and is set to be involved when they take on the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Sunday. Those players were nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon (shoulder), left tackle Theo Benedet (quad) and reserve running back Roschon Johnson (ankle). Kyler Gordon Battling Second Serious Injury of 2026 Season Getty Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon. Both Johnson and Benedet sustained their injuries during the game against New Orleans at Soldier Field on Sunday. Meanwhile, Gordon missed that contest due to a shoulder issue he suffered in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Chicago had a bye following that game, which means Gordon's injury has technically sidelined him for two weeks, as he would not have been healthy enough to play in Week 10 either. Gordon is a key piece of what the Bears do on defense, as his versatility as a slot cornerback renders him an effective player in blitz packages and in coverage alike. He missed the first five games of the year due to a calf strain, played big in four straight contests and has now sat one game with his shoulder injury and could miss the Bears' showdown with the Lions in Detroit coming off a short week. Gordon has tallied 13 combined tackles, including five tackles for loss, four sacks, four QB hits, two forced fumbles and a pass breakup in 139 defensive snaps played this season. Gordon's injury concerns stretch back to 14 missed games in 2025, and they have frustrated both the coaching staff and front office. His three-year, $40 million contract extension kicked in at the beginning of the 2026 campaign. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. home.headline: Dallas Cowboys' Injury Report Paints Promising Picture For Thanksgiving Game vs Eagles
home.blurb: On Monday, the team hit the practice field at The Star for a walkthrough, which gave us an early look at who could be in danger of missing the game, with the first injury report of the week . Luckily, there was nothing out of the ordinary. Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), star offensive lineman Tyler Booker (ankle), rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham (hip/groin), and linebacker Dee Winters (knee) were the four players who were held out of action. Winters was hurt during Sunday's win and was not expected to suit up, while the other three players have been out for the past week. For some positive news, we saw starting safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) return in limited fashion. Last week, the Dallas Cowboys' injury report was longer than a CVS receipt , so the first report for this week's game against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium is a positive sign. Dallas has a quick turnaround after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 , with just three days until returning to the field to face the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Jalen Thompson (hamstring), one of the team's biggest free agent signings) also improved and was a full participant as he inches closer to returning to action for the first time since Week 3. A full look at the first Cowboys injury report for Thanksgiving Week can be seen below. Dallas Cowboys' Week 12 Injury Report - Monday, November 23 Jake Ferguson, tight end (knee/ankle) Tyler Booker, offensive line (ankle) Jaishawn Barham, linebacker (hip/groin) P.J. Locke III, safety (concussion) Jonathan Mingo, wide receiver (ankle) Cobie Durant, cornerback (neck) Donovan Ezeiruaku, outside linebacker (ankle) Ottito Ogbonnia, defensive tackle (knee) Joey Porter Jr., cornerback (foot) Dak Prescott, quarterback (left hand) Jalen Thompson, safety (hamstring) Kickoff between the Cowboys and Eagles is set for 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. home.headline: Cowboys announce Dak Prescott injury update before Eagles game
home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys received an encouraging update regarding quarterback Dak Prescott ahead of their Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Dallas Cowboys put together their most impressive offensive performance of the 2026 NFL season on Sunday, defeating the Tennessee Titans 51-30 to improve to 5-6. Quarterback Dak Prescott continued his remarkable stretch of football, throwing for 325 yards and four touchdowns while adding another score on the ground. It marked the second consecutive game in which Prescott accounted for five touchdowns. Despite the Cowboys’ losing record, they remain within striking distance of the NFC East lead with six regular-season games remaining. However, there was some concern surrounding Prescott following Sunday’s victory. The veteran quarterback appeared at his postgame press conference with his left hand wrapped after suffering an injury against Tennessee. With a short turnaround before Thursday’s divisional game against the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas provided an encouraging update on Monday. Cowboys Provide Encouraging Dak Prescott Injury Update Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer eased concerns surrounding his franchise quarterback on Monday. When addressing Prescott’s injury , Schottenheimer delivered a straightforward four-word response. The Cowboys subsequently listed Prescott as a full participant on their estimated Monday injury report despite the left hand injury. Dallas held a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice. Prescott also downplayed the injury following Sunday’s win, explaining that his fingers had been bent backward during a hit against Tennessee. The development is particularly encouraging considering how well Prescott has played recently. The 33-year-old quarterback became just the fourth player in NFL history to record at least 300 passing yards and five total touchdowns in consecutive games, joining Tom Brady, Ben Roethlisberger and Daunte Culpepper. Dallas can ill afford to lose its quarterback as it attempts to climb back into the postseason picture. The Cowboys defeated Philadelphia 38-21 in their first meeting this season. Another victory over the Eagles would give Dallas a season sweep of its longtime rival. Philadelphia enters the game following a 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. However, the Eagles have injury concerns of their own, particularly in the secondary. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Jonathan Jones were both listed as nonparticipants on Monday’s estimated injury report. That could present opportunities for Prescott and his talented receiving duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. But this time it will be different! Remember, a broken clock is right twice a day. Anyway, Detroit will have a few challenges in this one, including facing a tough Tampa Bay defense a week after having to play a game in Germany. The Lions’ explosive offense had trouble generating points against Green Bay, Minnesota, and Miami (the Dolphins!) before bouncing back against the Patriots last week. Perhaps Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could use some of those blueprints to slow down star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Also, this will be the Lions’ first game without star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who sustained a season-ending knee injury against the Patriots. Peter Dewey Week 11 Upset Pick Baltimore Ravens (+114) vs. Carolina Panthers If you’re going to make a case for an upset this week where there are five teams favored by double digits, I don’t mind targeting the Baltimore Ravens in their clash with the Carolina Panthers. Carolina barely came away with a win over a bad New Orleans team in Week 10, and it remains pretty banged up on both sides of the ball. The Panthers are a top-10 team in the league in EPA/Play on offense, but they’re in the middle of the pack in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball. Carolina is also allowing 4.4 yards per carry on the ground, so this could be the week Derrick Henry gets going. The Ravens are coming off a pretty huge loss at home against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night, but Jacoby Brissett wasn’t bad in that matchup, and he may have led this Baltimore team to a win had Zay Flowers not lost a costly fumble late in the fourth quarter. I don’t think that any team in the NFC South should be trusted as a favorite, as the division as a whole is just 4-17 against the AFC North over the last four seasons and 63-111 overall against non-NFC South teams during that stretch. Iain MacMillan Week 11 Upset Pick The Lions' already bad and injured defense continues to take big hits. Now it's their star pass-rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the season after celebrating a sack against the Patriots on Sunday. He joins a list that includes D.J. Reed, Kerby Joseph, Devin White, and Jack Campbell, who are on the injured list. It's enough to convince me that now is the time to sell your Lions' stock. Detroit now has to take on a Buccaneers team that's fresh off a BYE week, and that ranks in the top five in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. While the Lions' offense is certainly elite, they're going to struggle to rack up the amount of points they need to aid their limping defense. Baker Mayfield's injury status is up in the air, which could make this bet tough to win, but if he plays, we're in a great spot. Even if he doesn't, Tampa Bay can win this game with their defense and rushing attack alone. They're my upset pick of the week. Week 12 Waiver Wire 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 Andrew Hughes · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:23 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come out of their bye at 3-6, and they've lost six games by seven points or fewer . A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. home.headline: Pat Summerall's 1952 Lions NFL championship ring is up for auction
home.blurb: Not many people can say they own a Detroit Lions NFL championship ring. The ring once owned by legendary broadcaster Pat Summerall, who played briefly for the Lions during his rookie season, is up for auction. The ring, from the Lions' 1952 championship, has been in Summerall's family until now. The ring is part of Lelands fall auction, and bidding is under way HERE . The reserve price was $5,000, and as of 1 p.m. Monday, Nov. 23, the bidding was up to $5,500. The auction ends Saturday, Dec. 5. The 1952 world championship ring is 14-karat gold with a single diamond in the center. The ring, made by Jostens, reads, "WORLD CHAMPIONS," with the year stamped to the left and right of the diamond. Summerall's name is engraved on the inside of the ring, which reads "LIONS" on the left and "NATIONAL FOOTBALL LEAGUE" on the right. The ring is a size 12.5, and was presented to Summerall after the Lions' 17-7 win over the Cleveland Browns in the 1952 NFL Championship Game. Summerall didn't play in the championship game, as the placekicker and defensive end got hurt early in the year. He did help the team on the practice squad during the season. The 1952 NFL championship was one of four won by the Lions, the last coming in 1957. The Lions, famously (infamously?), have never played in a Super Bowl. After the 1952 season, the Lions traded Summerall to the Chicago Cardinals, with whom he played five seasons. He finished his NFL career with four seasons with the New York Giants. After his playing days, Summerall became a prominent sports broadcaster, as the longtime partner of John Madden on NFL games. Summerall worked 16 Super Bowls on television and also called majors for tennis and golf, including 26 Masters. Summerall worked for CBS, Fox and ESPN during his broadcasting career. Summerall died April 16, 2013, at the age of 82. His daughter is Susie Wiles, President Trump's former chief of staff. Also part of the Lelands fall auction is a baseball signed by Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his Tyler, Texas, team that finished runner-up in the Junior League World Series in Taylor, Mich. Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that. Patrick Mahomes has finally shaken off the early rust coming off his torn ACL and LCL, and this squad is now playing some of its best football all year. Due to the lopsided nature of this particular game, the medical staff is in no rush to get Kenneth Walker III (groin) back on the field. Rookie tailback Emmett Johnson should continue to handle a large offensive workload, which he has undoubtedly earned with 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns last week. The Chiefs will face every team from the NFC West this season and have already played Seattle. They still have the Rams and 49ers after this weekend, which will serve as the final interconference matchups on the schedule. away.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

away.headline: Cardinals find troubling injury report surprise ahead of Chiefs game
away.blurb: Beck was officially listed as limited for practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, with a back injury. He was later present in the locker room while it was open to reporters, and appeared to be walking around without discomfort. The injury report was first released shortly after the locker room closed to reporters. This is not the first time Beck has had back trouble this season, as he dealt with a back injury for two weeks in October. That injury first surfaced on Oct. 16. He missed two practices the following week and was listed as a limited participant three times, before returning to full participation on Oct. 29. Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then. If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week. The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. “He’s just dealing with a bit of spasms,” head coach Mike LaFleur said on Oct. 23, of Beck’s previous injury. “It’s not like a long-term (issue) or anything like that. But trying to throw the way these guys throw, if you’re having a little bit of a back tweak, that’s what’s going on with him.” LaFleur’s next press conference is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, two days before the Cardinals’ game against the Chiefs in Kansas City. The bigger concern, though, would be the impact on Beck’s development, after an encouraging NFL debut in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams. home.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
home.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

home.headline: Cardinals find troubling injury report surprise ahead of Chiefs game
home.blurb: Beck was officially listed as limited for practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, with a back injury. He was later present in the locker room while it was open to reporters, and appeared to be walking around without discomfort. The injury report was first released shortly after the locker room closed to reporters. This is not the first time Beck has had back trouble this season, as he dealt with a back injury for two weeks in October. That injury first surfaced on Oct. 16. He missed two practices the following week and was listed as a limited participant three times, before returning to full participation on Oct. 29. Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then. If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week. The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. “He’s just dealing with a bit of spasms,” head coach Mike LaFleur said on Oct. 23, of Beck’s previous injury. “It’s not like a long-term (issue) or anything like that. But trying to throw the way these guys throw, if you’re having a little bit of a back tweak, that’s what’s going on with him.” LaFleur’s next press conference is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, two days before the Cardinals’ game against the Chiefs in Kansas City. The bigger concern, though, would be the impact on Beck’s development, after an encouraging NFL debut in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Week 12 Waiver Wire Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. away.blurb: On Monday, the Steelers were left wondering if Metcalf will be available to suit up against the Broncos on Black Friday — but the NFL announced it won't be taking any actions that would prevent that. The NFL's decision not to suspend Metcalf doesn't necessarily mean the Steelers couldn't decide to take team action by benching the wide receiver. However, at minimum, the league won't be preventing Metcalf from playing in Week 12. DK Metcalf's disappointing 2026 season continued with an unceremonious exit from the Steelers ' 19-16 loss to the Eagles on Sunday. The two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver was ejected from the Week 11 contest after attempting to poke Philadelphia cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. Metcalf had already been flagged for unnecessary roughness in the first half after getting physical with multiple Eagles players, and his third-quarter clash with DeJean resulted in an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and ejection. Metcalf had just one reception on four targets for two yards before heading to the locker room. Will DK Metcalf be suspended after ejection in Steelers' loss vs. Eagles? Metcalf will not be suspended by the NFL for his ejection and interactions with DeJean, according to Adam Schefter . However, his conduct "still will be reviewed for discipline in the form of fines." The NFL initially said it would review Metcalf's actions with the possibility of a suspension, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . "The NFL will review his ejection for additional penalties. That is what we know right now," Rapoport said during an appearance on Monday's edition of "Good Morning Football." "There are times when a player gets ejected, let's say earlier in a game, you say, 'OK, this is basically his punishment.' "There are other times, especially with ejections later in the game, where players do face additional penalties such as suspensions. That is where Metcalf is, so the NFL will evaluate and have an answer later [on Monday]." Metcalf has been ejected from a game three times in his NFL career. home.headline: Dallas Cowboys' Injury Report Paints Promising Picture For Thanksgiving Game vs Eagles
home.blurb: On Monday, the team hit the practice field at The Star for a walkthrough, which gave us an early look at who could be in danger of missing the game, with the first injury report of the week . Luckily, there was nothing out of the ordinary. Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), star offensive lineman Tyler Booker (ankle), rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham (hip/groin), and linebacker Dee Winters (knee) were the four players who were held out of action. Winters was hurt during Sunday's win and was not expected to suit up, while the other three players have been out for the past week. For some positive news, we saw starting safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) return in limited fashion. Last week, the Dallas Cowboys' injury report was longer than a CVS receipt , so the first report for this week's game against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium is a positive sign. Dallas has a quick turnaround after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 , with just three days until returning to the field to face the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Jalen Thompson (hamstring), one of the team's biggest free agent signings) also improved and was a full participant as he inches closer to returning to action for the first time since Week 3. A full look at the first Cowboys injury report for Thanksgiving Week can be seen below. Dallas Cowboys' Week 12 Injury Report - Monday, November 23 Jake Ferguson, tight end (knee/ankle) Tyler Booker, offensive line (ankle) Jaishawn Barham, linebacker (hip/groin) P.J. Locke III, safety (concussion) Jonathan Mingo, wide receiver (ankle) Cobie Durant, cornerback (neck) Donovan Ezeiruaku, outside linebacker (ankle) Ottito Ogbonnia, defensive tackle (knee) Joey Porter Jr., cornerback (foot) Dak Prescott, quarterback (left hand) Jalen Thompson, safety (hamstring) Kickoff between the Cowboys and Eagles is set for 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX. Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady will be in the booth to call the action at AT&T Stadium, while Pam Olivier and Tom Rinaldi will be keeping us updated from the sideline throughout the evening. home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles watched Riq Woolen return with Quinyon Mitchell and Jonathan Jones injured. Now the franchise learned the latter two’s status ahead of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Dallas Cowboys. Jones got ruled as a “did not practice” on Monday amid his ankle ailment . Meanwhile, Mitchell is dealing with a hamstring injury, keeping him out of practice. Dallas just dropped 51 points on the Tennessee Titans Sunday, marking the most points the Cowboys scored in a game since 2022 against the Indianapolis Colts. A Cowboys team led by former coach Mike McCarthy trounced Indy 54-19 back on Dec. 4, 2022. Dallas also blew out Philadelphia 51-26 that same season. So Philly may need to roll with Woolen in the secondary once again. But Dallas already lit up this Eagles secondary earlier in the season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Cowboys’ wide receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined to catch nine passes for 131 yards. Lamb scored two touchdowns while Pickens added one in the 38-21 trouncing back on Oct. 26 at Lincoln Financial Field. So these Cowboys are starting to hit their offensive stride. Quarterback Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns against the Titans and tallied 325 yards. Lamb delivered 132 yards and caught 11 passes in that same 21-point rout. But the Eagles are fresh off producing an emotional 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers . The win did more than hand Philly victory No. 3 this season, but the Eagles also took down the AFC North’s second-best team heading into that Sunday showdown. home.headline: Cowboys announce Dak Prescott injury update before Eagles game
home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys received an encouraging update regarding quarterback Dak Prescott ahead of their Thanksgiving Day game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Dallas Cowboys put together their most impressive offensive performance of the 2026 NFL season on Sunday, defeating the Tennessee Titans 51-30 to improve to 5-6. Quarterback Dak Prescott continued his remarkable stretch of football, throwing for 325 yards and four touchdowns while adding another score on the ground. It marked the second consecutive game in which Prescott accounted for five touchdowns. Despite the Cowboys’ losing record, they remain within striking distance of the NFC East lead with six regular-season games remaining. However, there was some concern surrounding Prescott following Sunday’s victory. The veteran quarterback appeared at his postgame press conference with his left hand wrapped after suffering an injury against Tennessee. With a short turnaround before Thursday’s divisional game against the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas provided an encouraging update on Monday. Cowboys Provide Encouraging Dak Prescott Injury Update Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer eased concerns surrounding his franchise quarterback on Monday. When addressing Prescott’s injury , Schottenheimer delivered a straightforward four-word response. The Cowboys subsequently listed Prescott as a full participant on their estimated Monday injury report despite the left hand injury. Dallas held a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice. Prescott also downplayed the injury following Sunday’s win, explaining that his fingers had been bent backward during a hit against Tennessee. The development is particularly encouraging considering how well Prescott has played recently. The 33-year-old quarterback became just the fourth player in NFL history to record at least 300 passing yards and five total touchdowns in consecutive games, joining Tom Brady, Ben Roethlisberger and Daunte Culpepper. Dallas can ill afford to lose its quarterback as it attempts to climb back into the postseason picture. Dak Prescott, Cowboys Face Important Thanksgiving Day Game Thursday presents an opportunity for Dallas to get back to .500 while picking up another important divisional victory. The Cowboys defeated Philadelphia 38-21 in their first meeting this season. Another victory over the Eagles would give Dallas a season sweep of its longtime rival. Philadelphia enters the game following a 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. However, the Eagles have injury concerns of their own, particularly in the secondary. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Jonathan Jones were both listed as nonparticipants on Monday’s estimated injury report. That could present opportunities for Prescott and his talented receiving duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. With several defensive players getting healthy, Carolina hosts the Baltimore Ravens , who have lost five straight games, most recently to the Chargers. away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. However, Carolina downgraded Brooks from questionable to out on Saturday, keeping Chuba Hubbard and Trevor Etienne as the team's top two running backs in Week 11 against the Baltimore Ravens. Panthers downgraded RB Jonathon Brooks to out for Sunday’s game vs. the Ravens due to his groin injury. That led to a conversation about Brooks' availability, and it appears the young running back is the odd man out in Carolina at the moment. Is Jonathon Brooks Playing Today? Canales admitted this week that the team is comfortable with Etienne as the backup and mentioned that both he and Anthony Tyus III can play special teams roles. Canales said he needs to speak with GM Dan Morgan about Jonathon Brooks’ availability. away.headline: Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status
away.blurb: While Jackson has not been officially ruled out for the season, he is expected to be sidelined for an extended period of time, and based on Baltimore's trajectory, it might be too late if and when he does actually return. While a Jackson trade seems incomprehensible, it might not be out of the realm of possibility. The 29-year-old has missed extensive time due to injuries the last two seasons. He sat out four games in 2025, and Baltimore ended up missing the playoffs. This year, he has played in just three contests. Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL MLB players' union blasts proposal Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It certainly has not been an easy year for Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Jackson missed three games early on in the 2026 NFL campaign due to an ankle injury. Then, after returning in Week 8, he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive snap, which ultimately resulted in surgery. Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork provided an update on Jackson's status Thursday, and unfortunately, he didn't seem to have anything substantial to add. "He's been in and he's focused on his rehab right now," Woolfork told The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec . What is Lamar Jackson's future with the Baltimore Ravens? Oct 4, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) drops back to pass during the first half against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Some have wondered if Jackson's time in Baltimore could be coming to an end. The two-time MVP is nearing the climax of a five-year, $260 million deal with the club, one that ends after 2027. There has been speculation that the Ravens could potentially look to trade Jackson before extending him. Given the clear wear-and-tear on Jackson's body, it is fair to wonder if parting ways would be the best thing for both sides this offseason. The Ravens' window seems to be closing, and with Jackson's health deteriorating, Baltimore might be better off starting from scratch. Whether or not it actually happens, of course, remains to be seen. home.headline: Panthers give injury update on WR Jalen Coker heading into Week 12
home.blurb: Carolina Panthers wideout Jalen Coker is all clear. The third-year receiver exited yesterday's 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens late in the fourth quarter. Coker took a big hit over the middle from linebacker Roquan Smith on a 6-yard reception, and was sent into concussion protocol. Head coach Dave Canales didn't have an immediate diagnosis on Coker following the victory—but he did provide the best update possible this afternoon, telling reporters that Coker has been cleared from protocol. Coker ended up with four receptions for 47 yards, his most since the team's Week 6 triumph over the Philadelphia Eagles. Most of that production came on a 35-yard catch in the first quarter, which set up the 23-yard touchdown grab by tight end Mitchell Evans a play later.
