Week 12 Waiver Wire Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 (James Lang-Imagn Images) Aiden Checketts · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers finally got in the win column as they picked up their first win of the season, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on the road on Monday Night Football. After winning their first game of the 2026 season, it is going to be interesting to see how LA approaches the rest of the season , and whether they are competitive or end up with a top draft pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, the focus now moves to their home matchup this week against the New York Jets in a game that could have a lot to do with how the draft order pans out. On that note, ESPN put out a Week 11 preview done by NFL Nation as well as fantasy football writer Eric Moody, analytics writer Seth Walder, and sports betting analyst Pamela Maldonado, who picked each game, and when it came to the Chargers and Jets matchup, LA was the unanimous pick. Now, in terms of the picks, Maldonado had the Chargers winning 24-20, Moody had a 23-17 victory for LA, and Walder picked Los Angeles to 23-20. All that to say, it is very clear that this ESPN panel does like the Chargers this week, and despite the fact the season has been rough for LA thus far, sometimes after picking up a win, a team can get into a rhythm and start stacking wins. One thing to note on the Chargers side, is the fact that they did a great job on the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball on Monday night against the Ravens. Starting with the defense, LA held running back Derrick Henry to 10 yards rushing on 10 carries and the Ravens 15 attempts for 16 yards as a team. That is a great performance for LA and because of that, it forced quarterback Jacoby Brissett to put the the game on his shoulders and the Chargers were able to do just enough to get the win through picking him off once and recovering a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers. Now on the offensive side, the Chargers ran the ball very well with running back Omarion Hampton tallying 22 carries for 105 yards and one score in addition to quarterback Justin Herbert adding seven carries for 51 yards and a touchdown. As a team, LA ran the ball 34 times for 160 yards while averaging 4.7 yards per carry. All that to say, the formula for the Chargers in Week 10 was dominating on both sides of the line of scrimmage which worked out and enabled them to pick up a win which was huge for their confidence, but also shows that they do not need to lean on Herbert. So, as the Chargers prepare to take on the Jets in Week 11, it will be interesting to see if LA can pick up another win, but also what the formula might be, because if Los Angeles once again dominates up front, that could be something that the Chargers can lean on for the rest of the year.

The Chargers beat a hobbled Baltimore Ravens team on Monday Night Football, and their short week to prepare for the next game showed. The Jets, who lost five games in a row until Sunday's victory, had been reeling and looked headed toward another bad season, though they improved to 3-8. The Chargers had two fumbles, but the Jets recovered neither. The Chargers' story of the game was their offensive line losing battles all the time. Justin Herbert was sacked six times, while Smith was taken down once, which ultimately proved to be the difference in the game. On run blocking, the Chargers' O-line did well, averaging more than five yards per carry, better than the Jets. What this loss means for the Chargers LA is still in the running to secure the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, currently sitting in second place. Herbert has played all six of his NFL seasons with the Bolts, who selected the ex-Oregon star with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft. His accolades includes the 2020 Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year award, a 2021 Pro Bowl nod and two ninth-place finishes in the NFL MVP race in 2022 and 2024. The Chargers largely struggled over Herbert's first four years save for a lone playoff appearance in 2022, although that wasn't the fault of the quarterback. Jim Harbaugh then arrived in town in 2024, and this team was much-improved in 2024 and 2025, going 11-6 with playoff appearances each season. However, the Chargers have endured a disastrous 2026 season, winning just once through 11 weeks. They are 0-5 at home after Sunday. Trey Lance is QB2 behind Herbert on the depth chart.

Justin Herbert Injury Update Causes Major Shift in Patriots vs. Chargers Odds for NFL Week 12 Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Los Angeles Chargers' 2026 season is already in the tank, as they've won just one of their first 10 games, and they received some awful news following Sunday's loss to the New York Jets. Quarterback Justin Herbert was placed in concussion protocol, putting his status for Week 12 against the New England Patriots in jeopardy. Originally, the Patriots and Chargers were supposed to play on Sunday night in Week 12, but the game was flexed with L.A. getting off to a slow start and Drake Maye (ankle) going down with potentially a season-ending injury in Week 10. Chargers QB Justin Herbert is now in concussion protocol. If Herbert is unable to go on Sunday, DJ Uiagalelei is the Chargers backup and would be in line to start against Tomm DeVito and the Patriots. That's quite the quarterback matchup, and Herbert's injury has shifted the odds for this game in a big way. L.A. was a 4.5-point favorite in the lookahead line for Sunday's game, but it dropped to just a 2.5-point favorite after losing to the Jets. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has moved the line even further, setting L.A. as a 1.5-point favorite at home with Herbert's status up in the air. It's a full three-point swing from the lookahead line, and the latest odds suggest that Herbert will miss Sunday's game. New England (5-5) is still in play to make the postseason in the AFC, even with DeVito at quarterback. The Patriots backup struggled in Week 10 against the Detroit Lions, but he may be able to upset Uiagalelei and the Chargers on Sunday. After all, the Chargers lone win came against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 and they've covered the spread in just one of their 10 games (1-8-1). Since the Chargers' season is basically over -- they have the worst Super Bowl odds in the NFL -- there's no reason to rush Herbert back into action to play on Sunday. Unfortunately for him, the Raiders don't have an effective run game to lean on, and their defense is a bottom-five unit. All signs point to the Broncos coming out of their BYE week hot against an inferior opponent. This is another tough game for Mendoza, as the Denver defense ranks amongst the top 13 teams in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play allowed and success rate this season. While the Bronco offense has struggled at times, this is a perfect “get-right” game, as the Raiders are allowing the most yards per play and have given up the second-most points in the NFL this season. Las Vegas’ inability to run the ball is also a major issue against a Denver secondary that is 11th in the league in EPA/Pass. Coming out of a bye, Sean Payton is 12-6 straight up in his career as a head coach. I expect him and the Broncos to make quick work of the Raiders as they look to jump ahead of Kansas City for the No. 1 spot in the AFC West. away.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders have been one of the healthier teams in the NFL this season, but they've finally started to deal with injuries. During the game, Adam Butler, Tim Keenan and JJ Pegues all had to leave due to injuries. Folorunso Fatukasi and Thomas Booker are the only remaining healthy defensive tackles on the active roster. To make matters even more concerning, Fatukasi and Booker were both on the injury report heading into Week 11. The Raiders are already soft at defensive tackle, so missing several players could be a big problem. Seventh-round pick Brandon Cleveland is on the practice squad, but he hasn't played a game this season. Chris Williams was active against the Broncos and will likely be elevated again. According to head coach Klint Kubiak, the Raiders are strongly considering signing another defensive tackle in free agency. "We've got guys that are on the practice squad that are going to have to step up," Kubiak told reporters on Monday. "We're gonna have to take a look outside and probably bring some guys in. That's where we're at right now. We've got to make sure that the guys that are coming in from the practice squad are ready to roll." It remains to be seen how serious the injuries are to the defensive tackles, but the Raiders would be wise to add at least one more. Veteran defensive tackle Larry Ogunjobi is currently a free agent. He has started 108 games in his career, so he's somebody who could step in and help. If the Raiders want somebody who is already on another team's practice squad, they could call up old friend Jihad Ward. He's currently on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, but could be poached if Las Vegas gives him an active roster spot. He was previously a second-round pick of the Raiders. Bilal Nichols is another former Raider who is currently a free agent. He has worked with defensive coordinator Rob Leonard before, so there's some familiarity. The team may also go with a younger player, as they clearly aren't in the playoff mix and could want to see if they can find an emerging young player instead of an aging veteran. Brandon Jones , however, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game after being a limited participant in practice all week long with a hamstring injury that he re-aggravated during Denver's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. They do have a spot open on the 53-man roster right now, and veteran safety Taylor Rapp could be a candidate to secure that spot, considering he's out of practice squad elevations. Jahdae Barron also played some safety against the Panthers and could be an option if Jones can't go. Tight end Caleb Lohner's 21-day window opened this week in practice, and there is no rush for Denver to necessarily bring him onto the active roster right away, which leaves his official status as out for Sunday's game by default. home.headline: Raiders Rule Out Important Starter vs. Broncos Due to Injury
home.blurb: Star tight end Brock Bowers is questionable, as is defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi and kicker Matt Gay. While those three still have a chance to play, the Raiders will be without a key starter. Starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway has been ruled out with a stinger injury. “They’ve really done a nice job,” Rizzi said. “They got obviously a whole new staff. [Special Teams Coordinator] Joe DeCamillis, who’s a name that’s recognized around here. Obviously he’s been a long time NFL special teams coordinator. I have a ton of respect for Joe. I’ve known Joe for a long time. Ironically, he was actually at Texas with my son a few years ago. So I think it starts with coaching. When you watch them on film, a huge emphasis in the phases. Then obviously the players, Dylan Laube’s having a phenomenal year as a kick returner, kind of leads the league. It’s not just the 95-yard touchdown. I feel like every time we watch the plays of the week, 40-yard return, 50-yard return, he’s got these chunk plays. Downhill runner, really tough, breaks tackles. So he’s done a really good job there. AJ Cole’s been one of the best punters in our league for the last five years or so. Not only is he punting the ball well, they’re covering well. So Joe’s done a really phenomenal job.” The post Raiders Rule Out Important Starter vs. Broncos Due to Injury appeared first on HEAVY . The Las Vegas Raiders are in desperate need of a win in Week 11 against the Denver Broncos. The team has lost six of its last seven and will have a really hard time getting back into the playoff race if it drops another game. Unfortunately, they’re set to face a 7-2 Broncos team that has been one of the top teams in the AFC for the last couple of seasons. The Raiders have been one of the healthier teams in the NFL this season, but are starting to get banged up. Hemingway has already missed one game this season, and this will be the second. He has been the Raiders’ best defensive tackle, so this is a big blow to the defense. The team is already terrible at stopping the run, so being without Hemingway is a problem. Sean Payton Discusses Klint Kubiak The Raiders have been at the bottom of the AFC West for a few years now, but head coach Klint Kubiak is hoping to turn things around. He’s still young in his career, but he’s already gained the respect of Broncos head coach Sean Payton. I have a ton of respect for their family and what he’s doing,” Payton said, via Raiders.com . “There are a lot of ties just to that organization. I think already you can see it on tape what they’re wanting to build and the early success this year. You go through Kansas City, Seattle, Buffalo, these are all teams that are in the thick of it, and they played all those teams to one-score games.” Raiders’ Special Teams Gets High Praise The Raiders’ offensive and defensive units have both been impressive this season, but the special teams have easily been the most consistent unit. Similarly, the Giants don't need to be told they're good, too. They do, after all, lead the NFC East, despite criticisms that the division is weak sauce. They are the only team in the division with a positive point differential (+7). They are also pretty angry about having blown a chance against the Washington Commanders last week, a loss that gives the third-place Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker if the two teams somehow end up with the same win-loss record at the end of the season. All of these factors have some critics snickering about the Giants' current standing. After all, someone has to be in first place, regardless of the division, right? And it's not that the Giants care what those outside of 1925 Giants Drive think about their team. Still, they can certainly make a statement with a convincing upset win over the Jaguars, who, surprisingly, FanDuel Sportsbook lists as only a 5.5-point favorite over Big Blue. Will the Giants come through and get their first home win since a 36-24 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 4, 2026? Let's dive in. Why the Giants Will Win The easiest way for the Giants to win this game is to keep the Jaguars offense off the field. And it just so happens that the Giants are currently second in the league in average time of possession (32:26), behind the league-leading Chicago Bears (34:31). That's not bad considering the Giants' rushing game ranks 18th in the league (112.6 yards per game). Big Blue averages 5.7 plays per drive, tying it for seventh in the league (Jacksonville averages 5.8 plays per drive, for those wondering). The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. Defensively, the Giants have been strong against the deep ball, which just so happens to be Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence's superpower. Lawrence has a 51.6 percent completion rate on passes of 20-plus air yards this season, fifth in the league. The Giants have a 38.4 percent blitz rate this season, fourth in the league, and have blitzed on 50 percent or more of their plays since Week 4, a 20 percent increase from the first three weeks. In terms of coverage, the Giants lead the league with a 17.2 percent completion rate allowed on deep balls of 20-plus air yards. They are also the only team not to allow a touchdown on a deep pass attempt, and they have four interceptions on those passes, tied for second in the league. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Jaguars Two potential reasons could doom the Giants' chances of scoring their first home win in over a month. The first is turnovers. The opportunistic Jaguars lead the league with a +9 turnover differential, having 16 takeaways to only seven giveaways. The Jaguars' takeaways include 12 interceptions ( fourth in the league ). The Giants currently have a -2 turnover differential, 21st in the league. They have three giveaways in their last three games (one interception and two lost fumbles). Fumbling has been an issue for the Giants, who have had six fumbles in their last two games. That's not good against an opportunistic Jacksonville team that is averaging 2.3 takeaways over its last three games. Give the Jaguars a short field to work with, and that's asking for trouble. The other thing to watch is the Jaguars' first-half scoring. The Jaguars lead the league in first-half scoring, averaging 15.89 points within the first 30 minutes of regulation. The Giants, meanwhile, have averaged 9.44 points per game in the first half. Needless to say, the Giants do not want to get into a situation where, late in the third or early in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars are so far ahead that Lawrence and other key starters get the rest of the afternoon off. This time, that test is set to come in the form of the 5-3-1 New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in a game that is set to consist of plenty of rain, and plenty of physical trench play. The Jaguars have answered almost every challenge that has come their way during the Liam Coen era, and this is another chance to meet the high expectations and standards that the Jaguars have created. "But any given Sunday—the NFL is the NFL. I was with the Rams in ‘22 when you lost to the 0-13 Jets. It is any given Sunday, anything can happen. And I do think our group believes that. They know that," Coen said on Friday. "I think they're a little bit ticked, especially on the defensive side from some of the things that happened on Sunday that wasn't up to our standard. So, I think when you have a hungry group that feels as if they have not done anything yet. Nothing. We're in the second half of the season. A lot to prove, a lot of work, more games to be played than we even just did and went through. We have new additions now where this is our football team. This is an opportunity as we move forward throughout these next few weeks to go and put it on tape with this team, our final football team of who we are for the rest of the season. Let's go put together four quarters of our best because we have yet to do it yet.” So, how do the national predictions see this one playing out as the Jaguars make a push in the AFC? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jaguars Matt Verderame: Giants Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Giants Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Giants Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars are once again seen as the overwhelming favorites entering this game, earning 27-of-30 votes to win. ESPN's Seth Wickersham is picking against the Jaguars for a second week in a row after, for some reason, picking the Tennessee Titans last week . I respect a good bit when I see it, and that is quite the bit. But as a whole, the Jaguars are the favorites because they are simply one of the best teams in the entire NFL. The Giants have been better than expected this season, though their wins have come against teams with losing records, and they are 0-1-1 against the powerhouse that is the 2026 Washington Commanders. They are a solid team, but the Jaguars have been on a different tier this season. The Jaguars enter Week 11 as the only team that ranks top-5 in both points per game (29.9, 4th) and points per game allowed (16.0, 2nd), leading the NFL with a +125 point differential. Jacksonville's point differential through nine games is the franchise's best since 1999 (+137). The Jaguars are 7-2 or better through nine games for the third time in franchise history, joining 1998 and 1999, the only seasons they won consecutive division titles. Offensively, the Jaguars will have to find a way to beat the blitz as the Giants send pressure at some of the highest rates in the entire NFL. The Jaguars' offense has hit big plays against the blitz this season, but they have not been as effecient down-to-down as they have when defenses are just sending four pass-rushers. Defensively, the Jaguars will need their new defensive pieces to make an impact. Jessie Bates III is set to start at safety and Jordan Davis is set to start at nose tackle, with each player set to potentially give the Jaguars a boost. Bates can help the Jaguars with turnovers and limiting big plays, while the Jaguars will need Davis right off the bat to make an impact against the Giants' running game. The Giants should give the Jaguars more of a test than most teams have had in recent weeks, but I still got the Jaguars in this one. Jaguars 27, Giants 17. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. Week 12 Waiver Wire NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. home.headline: Greg Newsome injury: NY Giants CB out multiple weeks with ankle injury
home.blurb: New York Giants starting cornerback Greg Newsome will be out multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday. Newsome left Sunday’s 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars after playing only four snaps. He was replaced by Paulson Adebo, who ended up with an interception and four passes defensed. “It’s a serious high ankle,” Harbaugh said. “It’s going to be one of those lengthy high ankles. Gonna be multiple weeks.” Harbaugh did not say whether Newsome would undergo surgery or be placed on injured reserve. A 2021 first-round pick by the Cleveland Browns, Newsome signed a one-year contract with the Giants in free agency this past offseason after a couple of sub-par years with the Browns and Jaguars. The 26-year-old has had a resurgent season with the Giants. His passer rating against of 67.3 is the best of his six-year NFL career. His completion percentage against of 57.9 is just a percentage point off his career-best. Newsome was rewarded with a three-year, $45.75 million contract extension recently. That deal runs through the 2029 season.

home.headline: Giants' Cam Skattebo Explains Backflip Despite Plans to Stop Celebration After Hutchinson's Injury
home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrated his team's 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars by doing something he said he said he wouldn't do again: a backflip. "When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo told reporters after the game. "I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. So when that happens, it's second nature and it's hard to hold back from." Skattebo planned on retiring the backflip after watching Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffer a season-ending knee injury on a celebration, but he couldn't resist the urge after clinching New York's victory with a 5-yard run. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
home.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. The Bengals keep rolling. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. away.headline: Colton McKivitz Suffers Gruesome Leg Injury, Latest on 49ers OL After Being Carted Off vs. Vikings
away.blurb: San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome leg injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the season after he was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. "It's brutal," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner . "He's somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He's the standard, and we're going to really miss him. We all love him. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sent his well wishes upon seeing the injury. The injury comes amid what has been a career year for McKivitz, who has the second-best PFF run block grade among tackles and the seventh-best overall grade among tackles. McKivitz has been a starter on the Niners' offensive line and has played all 17 games of the season since 2023. He has yet to miss a game this season, though that streak will surely come to an end. While McKivitz has established himself as a starter, the 30-year-old has had a long road to get to that point. He was a fifth-round draft pick in 2020 and started a handful of games as a rookie, but was waived ahead of the 2021 season, and had to work his way back onto the active roster via the practice squad. Eventually, he earned the job as a full-time starter ahead of the 2023 campaign, and he's stayed there ever since. away.headline: NFL-49ers rout Vikings as NFL makes electrifying return to Mexico
away.blurb: MEXICO CITY, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The San Francisco 49ers overwhelmed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday at the Azteca Stadium, as the National Football League made a thrilling return to Mexico City after a four-year absence with its first international Sunday Night Football game. The halftime show featured Mexican rock trio The Warning, as the break was extended by six minutes to accommodate the teams' return from locker rooms located outside the stadium. By Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina More than 85,000 fans, most of them backing the 49ers, filled the stadium, underlining the popularity of the sport in Mexico, which is the NFL's largest market outside the US. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell had described the occasion as a "mini-Super Bowl", underlining the importance of a country that has hosted five previous regular-season games since the league first played in Mexico in 2005. San Francisco quickly gave its supporters something to cheer when tight end George Kittle opened the scoring on the 49ers' first possession. Kittle, one of the most popular players among Mexican fans, added another touchdown in the second quarter, his fourth in the Mexican capital. "It was a complete home-field advantage. It was 97% Niners fans. They cheered the entire game: Let's go, Niners," Kittle told reporters. "But it was fantastic from start to finish. One of my favorite memories from this game will be the national anthem and the entire crowd singing. It gives me goosebumps. I love playing here, and I love the fans. It's some of the best energy I've ever felt." Minnesota responded with an 11-yard touchdown run by Aaron Jones but struggled to cope with San Francisco's offense and the deafening noise inside the stadium. The 49ers extended their lead through a touchdown pass from quarterback Brock Purdy to Mike Evans before safety Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned the ball 18 yards for a touchdown to make it 28-10 at halftime. The 49ers' right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field on a stretcher after suffering a lower-leg injury in the second quarter, prompting an emotional reaction from teammates. "We think it's broken, dislocated. Similar to probably Fred's last year. That was really crushing. Colton's had an unbelievable year," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan told a press conference. Purdy cemented his status as an MVP contender with a dominant performance against a Minnesota defense that had entered the game allowing an NFL-best 14 points per contest. away.headline: 7 winners and 3 losers from San Francisco 49ers' statement win over Vikings as Brock Purdy dismantles NFL's top defense
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The 49ers overwhelmed Minnesota behind a brilliant Brock Purdy performance and Mike Evans’ spectacular return, but one devastating injury threatens to overshadow the win. This one got out of hand quickly. The 49ers controlled it from the opening drive, and the Vikings never found an answer. There were plenty of standouts, but a few spots left room for concern. Here are the winners and losers from a decisive San Francisco win. Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdown passes, good for a 146 passer rating. Minnesota brought pressure, and it didn’t matter. Purdy threw with great anticipation and accuracy, per usual, and made a few plays out of structure on the move like we’ve seen every week. Look, if anyone still doubts this guy, I’m not sure what else he has to show them. Now, a 9-1 record speaks for itself, but beating Minnesota like this means more than one win. The 49ers went into Mexico City against one of the conference’s best teams and the league’s top defense, and they beat the Vikings by 25. The McKivitz injury is the one real worry coming out of this one. With Purdy playing at this level and Evans back in the lineup, I believe San Francisco is the team to beat in the NFC. Could the San Francisco 49ers have made a louder statement in Mexico City? Not really. San Francisco throttled the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 and moved to 9-1, pulling away from one of the NFC’s top teams and doing it against what might be the best defense in football. Kittle set the tone with the opening-drive touchdown. He added a second score in the first half, catching a pass over the middle and ripping it away from Vikings safety Harrison Smith. He finished with three receptions for 34 yards and two touchdowns. The yardage won’t jump off the page, but Kittle was a matchup problem in the red zone all night. The San Francisco 49ers have a 98% chance to make the NFL playoffs and a 13% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Sun, Nov 22). Evans returned from his Achilles injury for the first time since Oct. 19 against the Commanders, and he picked up right where he left off. He caught six passes for 109 yards and a touchdown, and that score was a crazy one-handed grab in the back corner of the end zone. Getting his top receiver back makes Purdy and this offense far more dangerous. Brown jumped a slant over the middle late in the first half, picked off Kirk Cousins, and took it to the house. That pick-six swung the game. Minnesota had a chance to keep it close, and Brown made the Vikings quarterback pay instead. Lenoir had a tougher time last week while facing Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens for most of the game. This week, he answered. He followed Justin Jefferson for most of the night, broke up two passes, and then made a huge play late. Lenoir forced a fumble on Jefferson after the catch and recovered it himself. Holding one of the league’s best receivers in check is how a corner earns trust

He finished with three receptions for 34 yards and two touchdowns. The yardage won’t jump off the page, but Kittle was a matchup problem in the red zone all night. The San Francisco 49ers have a 98% chance to make the NFL playoffs and a 13% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Sun, Nov 22). Evans returned from his Achilles injury for the first time since Oct. 19 against the Commanders, and he picked up right where he left off. He caught six passes for 109 yards and a touchdown, and that score was a crazy one-handed grab in the back corner of the end zone. Getting his top receiver back makes Purdy and this offense far more dangerous. Brown jumped a slant over the middle late in the first half, picked off Kirk Cousins, and took it to the house. That pick-six swung the game. Minnesota had a chance to keep it close, and Brown made the Vikings quarterback pay instead. Lenoir had a tougher time last week while facing Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens for most of the game. This week, he answered. He followed Justin Jefferson for most of the night, broke up two passes, and then made a huge play late. Lenoir forced a fumble on Jefferson after the catch and recovered it himself. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Monday night contest in DC Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals . Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival New York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks. Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night. Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough as kickoff is approaching. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Commanders vs. Bengals live Date: Monday, Nov. 23 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Northwest Stadium (Landover, Maryland) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -6, O/U 54.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bengals have the ball Joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL . Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease. Ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him. The Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment. Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample , though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two. Washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league. However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins. When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams . Without Terry McLaurin , Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs , rookie Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo. Diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position. The Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year. The Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler , each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football. With big Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins , Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground. The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. away.headline: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured vs Commanders Monday night
away.blurb: The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable. Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. "It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)." Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter. Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury. Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter. Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million. "My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life." Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament. Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022. away.headline: Commanders Week 11 injury report vs. Bengals for MNF: 4 players listed as questionable
away.blurb: Commanders Week 11 injury report vs. Bengals for MNF: 4 players listed as questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Washington Commanders are scheduled to wrap up Week 11 with a " Monday Night Football " matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals . It's a game that gives Washington a chance to earn its fourth win of the season, after going 3-5-1 to begin the campaign. However, the team is dealing with several injuries on the roster, with four players deemed questionable going into the contest. Here's everything we know about those four players, and more. The Commanders have 13 total players on the injury report heading into Monday's outing against the Bengals. But four already have their status listed as questionable : running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, offensive lineman Lucas Patrick, cornerback Amik Robertson, and running back Rachaad White. Jacory Croskey-Merritt – Groin: Questionable Lucas Patrick – Concussion: Questionable Amik Robertson – Ankle: Questionable Rachaad White – Heel: Questionable Swayze Bozeman – Forearm: Questionable Oren Burks – Groin: Out Jalen Davis – Hamstring: Doubtful Kyle Dugger – Quadriceps: Questionable Dylan Fairchild – Oblique: Questionable Daxton Hill – Illness: Questionable Andrei Iosivas – Thumb: Doubtful Brian Parker II – Knee: Questionable Dalton Risner – Knees: Out Commanders' Jacory Croskey-Merritt 'expected' to return from injury for Bengals matchup MLB players' union blasts proposal Benedetto Vitale, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Mon, November 23, 2026 at 5:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Commanders Week 11 injury report vs. Bengals Croskey-Merritt has not played since the club's 27-27 overtime tie with the New York Giants in Week 5. The 25-year-old has been dealing with a groin injury that has forced him to miss the past four games. Washington just recently activated Croskey-Merritt from the IR in the week leading up to the game against the Bengals. This season, he's accumulated 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 rush attempts. Considering the team is 3-5-1 on the season entering Week 11, Washington needs as many healthy bodies as possible to have a chance against Joe Burrow and the Bengals. At the very least, Jayden Daniels has been playing well since returning from his elbow injury. But Washington will still want its players healthy against Cincinnati. home.headline: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured vs Commanders Monday night
home.blurb: The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable. Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. "It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)." Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter. Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury. Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter. Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million. "My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life." Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament. Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injures ankle vs Commanders Monday night

home.headline: Joe Burrow pops up on Bengals' first injury report ahead of Monday night showdown against Commanders
home.blurb: Linebacker Oren Burks (groin) and right guard Dalton Risner (knee) were the other DNPs, as foretold by coach Zac Taylor prior to practice . Burks isn't expected to practice all week, while Risner is considered day-to-day. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) and left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) were each limited Thursday. Dugger has been week-to-week for the last few weeks as he's still dealing with an injury from all the way back in Week 3. Fairchild suffered his injury in Week 9 and was able to play most of last week despite it. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) practice for the first time since Week 5 as he was designated to return off the Reserve/Injured list Thursday. Cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring), WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb), and G Brian Parker II (knee) remain full participants as they await activation to the 53-man roster . Bengals return to 53 players on their active roster with sensical moves before kickoff against Commanders Bengals wake up smiling following their Sunday off after multiple AFC foes help out their playoff positioning Bengals declare two players out against Commanders and another starter figures to be game-time decision Joe Burrow pops up on Bengals' first injury report ahead of Monday night showdown against Commanders Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The Cincinnati Bengals released their first injury report ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Washington Commanders. Quarterback Joe Burrow is one of a few Bengals dealing with an illness. Bengals' Thursday injury report for NFL Week 11 Joe Burrow isn't alone under the weather Quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was a full participant at practice, but the club announced during practice he is dealing with an illness and would not speak with reporters after practice. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took Burrow's place at his post-practice presser. “I don't know if he told y'all how he's feeling or not, but overall he looks good,” Chase said of Burrow while wearing his orange No. 9 practice jersey. “I think everybody around the team is just coming on with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good. Still feels the same.” He's not wrong. Starting cornerback Dax Hill and offensive tackle Myles Hinton are also dealing with illnesses. Hill wasn't able to practice at all. Hinton was a late add to last week's injury report with his illness and was a full participant Thursday. Burrow being able to practice fully Thursday is obviously good news for his prospects playing Monday. He's expected to address the media either Friday or Saturday. WR Tee Higgins (knee) and safety PJ Jules (ankle) were also full participants.
